A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical causal-gating RAG framework and HolisQA benchmark, with HugRAG renamed CausalRAG2. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results in Tables 3–4, component ablations, scalability experiments, and causal-gate retrieval measurements in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds gate-control comparisons, quantified expert validation, cost measurements, hyperparameter sweeps, and backbone stability results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes the score threshold tau and explicitly constructs undirected binary gates instead of scored directed gates. This is a limited specification correction: v1's Figure 9 already used binary judgments accepting either causal direction. The hierarchy, seeding, traversal, filtering, and generation stages remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five standard QA datasets and five HolisQA domains. The added studies reuse existing coverage, mainly HolisQA-CompSci; gate perturbations and backbone substitutions change internal configurations rather than the represented data or QA tasks.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. Appendix E.1 adds evaluated Random and Semantic gate-construction comparators, alongside false-positive and false-negative gate variants, in the new Table 6 comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a 500-question gate comparison with matched gate counts, four six-value hyperparameter sweeps, cross-backbone filtering evaluation using Jaccard similarity, and cost/latency measurements normalized per 1K corpus tokens and per query. These substantially extend the evaluation protocol; the retained main benchmarks keep their stated backbone and metrics.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing component ablations and gate on/off analysis with random-versus-semantic gate controls, 25% gate addition/removal tests, hyperparameter sensitivity, backbone stability, and quantified expert validation. Appendix D.2 also adds two cross-module retrieval cases. These address mechanism specificity, gate errors, reliability, and practical cost.

E5.justification: Appendix H.2 newly reports three filtering runs per backbone and mean pairwise Jaccard similarities. The expert audits also report inter-annotator agreement. Figure 13's existing 95% bootstrap confidence intervals are retained; no repeated-run uncertainty is added to the main benchmark tables.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 and the existing ablation and scalability results retain their values. Substantial new results include gate-comparison F1 scores of 31.62 for Causal, 23.86 for Random, and 24.87 for Semantic; query cost and latency of $0.00049 and 0.801 seconds; and sensitivity, stability, and expert-audit outcomes. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes the formal gate relation from directed pairs to unordered, non-self pairs. Appendix B.1 replaces the causal-transitivity justification for pruning with a reachability argument through parent gates and hierarchical edges. These revise the mathematical specification and reasoning without adding a substantial theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The central hierarchical-gating, retrieval-quality, and HolisQA contributions remain. V2's conclusion modestly broadens the claimed applicability to organizing long contexts and long-term memory for LLMs and agents. Mentioning HolisQA in the abstract promotes a contribution already present in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly identifies non-task-adaptive hierarchy construction and limited domain coverage as limitations. Appendix H.2 adds an interpretation linking filtering reliability to backbone capacity. Section 5.3 more explicitly explains the precision loss from structural expansion alone and relates gains over CausalRAG to graph heterogeneity.

D1.justification: V2 adds reported code and HolisQA access information, explicit Algorithm 1 function descriptions, the default hop decay of 0.7, expert-audit sampling and annotation details, and construction/query token, time, and cost breakdowns. Together these substantially expand practical reproducibility information. Appendix F.3 also removes v1's blanket statement that other baseline parameters use defaults.

R1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a broader positioning paragraph connecting the work to formal verification, uncertainty, typicality, and efficient AI systems, citing new works including VERGE, CausalGuard, and FORTE. The main RAG and causality positioning is retained; many other reference changes update metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: The paper consistently adopts CausalRAG2, edits terminology and several explanatory paragraphs, and adds organizational headings for sensitivity, cost, limitations, and expanded appendices. The original narrative and most prose remain recognizable; the added scientific material does not constitute an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables 5, 6, 9, and 10 substantially extend the displayed evidence with cost comparisons, gate variants, a detailed cost/token breakdown, and four sensitivity blocks. Table 9 expands the Table 5 summary. Existing figures are largely retained, with naming updates and relocation, while the original graph-statistics tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central mechanism. V1's gate on/off study could not separate causal selection from generic extra connectivity; v2 adds matched-count random and semantic controls, gate perturbations, and quantified expert audits, alongside cost and stability evidence. These address an important evidential gap while preserving the main results. Validation remains concentrated in HolisQA-CompSci, and Table 10 leaves differing default-setting scores unexplained, but the gains in mechanism validation clearly outweigh these limitations.
